title: fix(layout,types): an app-schema-renderer node draws the app document it carries under `schema` (objectui#11494)
body:
Fixes #11494

Clause-②: yes

An `app-schema-renderer` node now draws the app document it carries under `schema`, and `AppSchemaRendererNodeSchema` declares `schema` as that document, by reference. This executes triage ruling A (comment `5958227972`) on the card. The standing ruling that this node is "the one JSON door for 'render a whole shell from a schema'" (objectui#4841, `5307574602`) is unchanged. Builds on objectui#11440 (PR objectui#11493, landed as `00ccdf742`, this branch's base).

## What was wrong (measured at the base, `00ccdf742`)

`SchemaRenderer` strips a node's `schema` key out of the props it spreads, and hands every registered component the node itself as its `schema` prop. `registerLayout()` registered `AppSchemaRenderer` directly, so the component took the node for its app document. Rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry at the base, with this PR's new layout pin file and the source untouched:

- `{ type: 'app-schema-renderer', schema: { type: 'app', name: 'crm', navigation: NAV } }` drew no navigation: `expected 'App' to contain 'Accounts11494'`.
- The same navigation written flat on the node drew: `expected 'crmAccounts11494' not to contain 'Accounts11494'`.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/layout`** (`packages/layout/src/index.ts`): `app-schema-renderer` is registered against `AppSchemaRendererNode`, a module-private adapter in the `DetailSectionNode` shape. It reads `node.schema` off the node `SchemaRenderer` already hands it, and gives that to `AppSchemaRenderer`. Every other prop (`basePath`, `mobileNavMode`, host props) passes through unchanged. There is no fallback to the node's own keys. A node without `schema` hands the component an empty `{ type: 'app' }` document, which draws the shell with no branding and no navigation, as such a node drew before. `AppSchemaRenderer`, its props and the registration's `inputs` are unchanged.
- **`@object-ui/types`** (`packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`): `AppSchemaRendererNodeSchema` gains `schema: AppComponentSchema.optional()`. It is the same schema object, with no copy of its members.
- **`content/docs/guide/layout.md`**: the passage now says what the node does, with a JSON example (checked once by hand on both faces, see Gates). The `children` sentence ("takes the page content as its `children`"), which the probe did not reproduce, is replaced by what holds: the node's children are not rendered, and `objectui validate` refuses them on this node.
- **Tests**: two new pin files, the objectui#11440 rows moved on purpose, and two fixtures respelled to the nested form (below).
- **Changesets**: `@object-ui/types` minor and `@object-ui/layout` minor, the latter marked breaking for a node that writes app keys flat on itself.

## Contract notes (for the at-tier review)

- **Seam: the adapter reads `props.schema.schema`. `SchemaRenderer`'s strip list is not touched.** `SchemaRenderer` already delivers the whole node as `schema`, so no wider seam was needed. Nothing new is exported: the adapter is private to `index.ts`.
- **"By reference" means the nested document carries `"type": "app"`.** `AppComponentSchema` requires the `app` literal, so `{ schema: { name: 'crm' } }` is refused at `schema.type` (`invalid_value`). A typeless variant would be a derived schema (`.omit` / `.partial`), not the document by reference, so it was not taken. The TypeScript prop `AppSchemaRendererProps.schema` already requires `type: 'app'` of JSX hosts.
- **Accept set, per face.**
  - Strict face (`StrictAnyComponentSchema`): **widens**. A node with its document under `schema` validates; it was refused with `unrecognized_keys` naming `schema`. The nested document is closed like every object on this face (`schema.brading` is refused by name).
  - Tolerant face (`safeValidateSchema`, which `objectui validate` runs): `schema` used to pass unjudged and is now judged as the app document. A malformed nested value is refused: no `type: 'app'`, a non-object, or `mobileNavMode` inside the document (the objectui#11363 tombstone). That is a **narrowing for a malformed nested document** on this face. The producer reading below found no such document.
- **One spelling.** The document's keys written flat on the node stay undeclared. The strict face refuses them as `unrecognized_keys` (`navigation`, `title`), and the adapter does not read them. The tolerant face keeps its passthrough for them, so `objectui validate` alone does not refuse them. The guide says the strict face does, and nothing more.
- **Optional, not required.** The registration input is not `required`, and the node the governed mobile guide teaches (`{ type: 'app-schema-renderer', mobileNavMode: 'bottom_nav' }`) carries no document. It still validates on both faces, and still draws: both are pinned.
- **Producers.** objectstack at `4e6dc233`: `git grep app-schema-renderer` finds one hit, a CHANGELOG line, and no node producer (control word `page:header` hits in the same tree). objectui: no doc, example or catalog document authors the node with a document, flat or nested. The only authored nodes are test fixtures, two of them respelled here.
- **A pending changeset this PR makes false.** `.changeset/11440-arm-passing-types.md` (unreleased) says the registration's third input, `schema`, "is not declared". This PR's types changeset says that sentence no longer holds. The 11440 body is outside this claim's file surface and was not edited; the report names the correction.

## Pins

- `packages/layout/src/__tests__/app-schema-renderer-schema-input-11494.test.tsx`, through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry:
  - navigation under `schema` draws, and the same navigation flat on the node draws nothing;
  - `title` under `schema` heads the sidebar, and flat it does not;
  - `basePath` and `mobileNavMode` are unchanged: the bottom bar's tab is `/apps/crm/account`, and the `drawer` control draws no bar;
  - a node without `schema` draws the empty shell with no error banner;
  - the registration publishes `schema` as an object input, and the arm declares it.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/app-schema-renderer-schema-input-11494.test.ts`, on both faces, each refusal with a lit control:
  - the member unwraps to `AppComponentSchema` itself, and is optional;
  - a nested document validates beside `basePath` and `mobileNavMode`, and a node without `schema` validates;
  - flat keys are refused strict as `unrecognized_keys` (the same keys nested pass);
  - `mobileNavMode` inside `schema` is the app document's tombstone (on the node it is clean);
  - an untyped document is refused at `schema.type`, and the strict face closes the nested document.
- **Moved on purpose, under the ruling:** the objectui#11440 layout row "`schema` is an input the arm does not declare — and a node never delivers it to the component" (its file header now points at the 11494 file), and the types row "the registration's `schema` input is not declared" (now a one-line `toContain('schema')` with a pointer).
- **Fixtures respelled** (each only used the flat or untyped spelling): the node in `app-mobile-nav-mode-refusal-11363.test.ts` nests its document, so its comparisons run against a clean baseline on both faces. The schema-catalog control node's document gained `type: 'app'`; without it, that node is refused on both faces.

## Reverse verification

- **Predicted:** red at the base, and ablating the adapter turns exactly the four drawing rows red.
- **Base** (`00ccdf742`, source untouched, the new pin files only): `Tests  13 failed | 4 passed (17)`.
- **Ablation** on the committed fix, through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which reverts the registration to `AppSchemaRenderer`:
  - anchor count 1 to 0, blob `d66737e2b8e7` to `1391f799016e`;
  - `Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)`: the four drawing rows, as predicted;
  - restore: `blob == HEAD (d66737e2b8e7) and git diff HEAD is empty`.

## Gates (final head `44a67d8fc`)

- **Tests** (`pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/layout/ packages/types/`, plus the 15 tests outside those two packages that name `app-schema-renderer`, `AppSchemaRenderer`, `AppComponentSchema`, `mobileNavMode` or `layout.md`, plus `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts`): `Test Files  391 passed (391)`, `Tests  9710 passed (9710)`. That set includes the ratchet `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch, and the zod-parity and strict-face suites in `packages/types`.
- **Type-check**, `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/layout`: both scripts echoed `type-check: Done`, exit 0. They ran on `ebb7d21ba`; `git diff --stat ebb7d21ba HEAD -- packages/` is empty. `--listFiles` shows both test programs include the touched test files. `@object-ui/example-schema-catalog` type-check: exit 0 on `44a67d8fc`.
- `pnpm check:doc-snippets`, after its `--build-filter` closure build: `Semantic phase: 776 of 776 block(s) judged, 0 failed.` It ran on `25c91e58b`; only a test file changed after that.
- `pnpm check:doc-examples`: `Every covered @example compiles, or fails exactly as its ledger row declares.`
- `pnpm check:doc-types`: `Every documented component type is registered.`
- `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`: `115 candidate test files, all adjudicated; 82 declared entries, all present.`
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: `OK (scanned 10092 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).`
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `9 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 2 changeset(s)`.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: report-only, exit 0. It names 21 pending changesets that cite a touched file; each paragraph was read, and none is falsified. The one this PR does falsify (11440, above) names no file, so this gate cannot see it.
- **eslint** over the 9 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 9 files, 0 errors, 4 warnings, all on lines this PR does not touch (blame). Three facts prove the narrowing:
  - population: eslint itself answers "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied" for the 4 changed `.md` files;
  - count: the JSON output lists 9 files;
  - invariance: `--print-config` shows no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (not type-aware), and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- The guide's new JSON example, checked once against the built `@object-ui/types` dist (not a permanent test): tolerant `true`, strict `true`. With the document flat on the node: strict `false` (`unrecognized_keys` on `title`, `navigation`), tolerant `true`, which is what the guide says.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 13 paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.
- Patch round 1 (head `6d47fdb9e`): `AppSchemaRendererNodeSchema` is annotated with `AppSchemaRendererNodeSchemaType`, written by reference to `AppComponentSchema` (the `PageKindNodeSchemaType` precedent), so declaration emit names the nested document instead of re-serializing it inside `AnyComponentSchema`. Type only; the accept set is unchanged. `Spec Main Shape Gate` reproduced locally against objectstack `9b7a0ef3faf1`: red without the annotation (`index.zod.ts` 590 TS7056 x2), green with it. The pending objectui#11440 changeset carries a dated note.

## Acceptance notes

- `.changeset/11440-arm-passing-types.md` should drop the sentence that says the registration's third input, `schema`, "is not declared" and the strict face refuses it. Out of this claim's surface; the report names the replacement.
- The `children` / `body` refusal message on this node says `SchemaRenderer` strips both "out of the props it hands `AppSchemaRenderer`". The props now reach the adapter, which forwards no node children, so the sentence still holds in substance. It is published refusal text, and is left as it is.
- `packages/layout/README.md` ("the key for that is `app-schema-renderer`") stays true and is not edited.
- `objectui validate` runs the tolerant face, so flat app keys on this node pass it, as any undeclared key passes on any node. That is the two-face design objectui#5250 ruled, not this card's.
